---
title: "Set up"
subtitle: "About 10 minutes, plus a download. Do it before the session if you can; we'll also do it together at the start."
---

::: {.callout-note}
## What you need

- A Mac with macOS 14 (Sonoma) or newer, or a PC with Windows 10 (version 22H2) or Windows 11.
- About 10 GB of free disk space.
- Any amount of memory. The starter model runs on 8 GB.

On a Chromebook or a tablet, or on a computer that won't let you install apps? Come anyway. You'll see every step,
and you're welcome to just watch.
:::

## 1. Check your computer {#check}

Write these down. In the session, we'll use them to choose a second model that fits your computer.

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Mac

Open the Apple menu → **About This Mac**.

- **Chip:** Apple M1 or newer means Ollama uses the Mac's graphics, which is fast. An Intel chip works too, more
  slowly.
- **Memory:** for example, 16 GB.
- **macOS:** 14 (Sonoma) or newer.

### Windows

Open **Settings → System → About**, and note **Installed RAM**: for example, 16 GB.

Then press {{< kbd Ctrl-Shift-Esc >}} to open Task Manager, and click **Performance**. A GPU named **NVIDIA** or **AMD
Radeon RX** is a dedicated graphics card: note its **Dedicated GPU memory**. Only Intel graphics, or AMD Radeon
Graphics? Ollama runs on your processor instead: slower, but it works.
:::

## 2. Install Ollama {#install}

Ollama is a free app that downloads open AI models and runs them on your computer.

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Mac

1. Download [Ollama for Mac]({{< var ollama.mac >}}), about 230 MB. On
   [ollama.com/download]({{< var ollama.download >}}), it's the **Download manually** link under the command.
2. Open the downloaded file, **Ollama.dmg**, and drag **Ollama** into **Applications**.
3. Open **Ollama** from Applications. If it offers to install the command line tool, say yes. It may ask for your
   password.
4. When it asks you to sign in, choose **No thanks, I'll use Ollama locally**. You don't need an account.

A llama icon in the menu bar means Ollama is running.

### Windows

1. Download [Ollama for Windows]({{< var ollama.windows >}}), about 1.7 GB, so start it early. On
   [ollama.com/download]({{< var ollama.download >}}), it's the **Download manually** link under the command.
2. Run **OllamaSetup.exe**. It installs for your account only, so you don't need administrator rights.
3. When Ollama opens and asks you to sign in, choose **No thanks, I'll use Ollama locally**. You don't need an
   account.

A llama icon by the clock means Ollama is running.

### Linux

Run this in a terminal. It asks for your password (`sudo`) and needs the `zstd` tool; on Ubuntu, install it first
with `sudo apt install zstd`.

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh
```
:::

The chat app is for Mac and Windows. On Linux, use the terminal steps below.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Already have Ollama?

Update it: download the latest from [ollama.com/download]({{< var ollama.download >}}) and install it over the old
one. The starter model needs Ollama 0.30 or newer.
:::

## 3. Keep everything on your computer {#local}

Ollama can also run some models on its company's servers. Those are marked **cloud**, and your words leave your
computer when you use them. For this workshop, turn them off: in the Ollama window, open **Settings** and switch off
**Cloud** ("Enable cloud models and web search").

## 4. Download the starter model {#starter}

Open a terminal, a window where you type commands instead of clicking.

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Mac

Press {{< kbd Cmd-Space >}}, type **Terminal**, and press {{< kbd Enter >}}.

### Windows

Press the {{< kbd Win >}} key, type **PowerShell**, and press {{< kbd Enter >}}.
:::

Copy this line, paste it into the terminal, and press {{< kbd Enter >}}:

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
ollama pull {{< var starter.name >}}
```
:::

It downloads about {{< var starter.size >}}. It's done when it prints `success`. Then say hello:

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
ollama run {{< var starter.name >}} "Say hello in one sentence."
```
:::

**It works when** the model answers with a greeting, like `Hello there!`

Now try the app: in the Ollama window, choose **{{< var starter.name >}}** in the model menu and send it a message.

## 5. That's all until the session {#done}

There's no need to download other models: choosing one that fits your computer is part of the session. Ollama keeps
running quietly in the background. To stop it, click the llama icon and choose **Quit Ollama**.

## If something goes wrong

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `command not found: ollama` (Mac) | Open the Ollama app once and let it install the command line tool. Then open a new Terminal window. |
| `'ollama' is not recognized` (Windows) | Close PowerShell and open a new one. |
| `could not connect to ollama server` | Ollama isn't running. Open the Ollama app; the llama icon appears when it's ready. |
| `You need to be signed in to Ollama to run Cloud models.` | You chose a cloud model. Choose **{{< var starter.name >}}** instead. |
| The download is slow or stops | Run the same `ollama pull` line again. It picks up where it stopped. |
| The installer won't run on a university-managed computer | Ask your IT support, or watch along in the session. |
| Your Mac runs macOS 13 or older | This version of Ollama won't install. Update macOS, or watch along. |
| Not enough disk space | Free up about 10 GB. Models live in `~/.ollama/models` on a Mac and in `C:\Users\<you>\.ollama\models` on Windows. **Settings → Model location** can move them. |

<p class="small-muted">Checked against Ollama {{< var ollama.checked >}} on {{< var ollama.checked-date >}}. Ollama
changes often; if a screen looks different, the <a href="{{< var ollama.docs >}}">official docs</a> win. Help with
your own setup: <a href="{{< var help >}}">go.ncsu.edu/getdatahelp</a>.</p>
